paper.title: Stochastic Linear Bandits with Protected Subspace

settings.name_in_paper: Protected Linear Bandit with unit-ball action space
unmapped: Learner queries one of L+1 unknown vectors (target theta_0 or protected theta_1..theta_L) per round with its action and observes a noisy inner product; reward is <a, Proj^perp_{span(theta_1..theta_L)} theta_0>, never observed
Protected subspace has dimension s (< d), and the learner knows s
Regret depends on lambda_min, the best minimum nonzero eigenvalue of sum_{i in S} theta_i theta_i^T over spanning subsets of size s
settings.definition_quote: At every round $t$, the player can choose any action $A_t\in \mathcal{A}_t$, and an index $I_t\in \{0\}\cup [L]$, and receive a corresponding feedback of $X_t = \langle A_t, \theta_{I_t}\rangle +\eta_t$ ... $\mathcal{R}_{[T]} = \sum_{t\in [T]} \langle a^*_t-A_t, \Proj_{\{\theta_i\}_{i\in [L]}}^{\perp}\theta_0\rangle.$ ... The action space $\mathcal{A}_t$ at all times consists of all vectors with unit norm, i.e. $\mathcal{A}_t =\mathcal{B}^2_d$

settings.name_in_paper: Protected Linear Bandit with finite (time-varying) action space (lower bound)
unmapped: Learner queries one of L+1 unknown vectors per round and observes a noisy inner product; reward is the projection of theta_0 orthogonal to the protected span, never observed
Action set each round drawn i.i.d. from two finite sets with equal probability
settings.definition_quote: In both instances, in each round, we allow the player an action space that consists of either the actions $\{u_{\pi-\alpha}, u_{2\alpha}\}$ or $\{u_{\pi-\alpha}, u_{2\alpha}, u_{\pi-3\alpha}\}$ with equal probability.

symbols.s_prot: dimension of the protected subspace (known to the learner)
symbols.lambda_min: largest over size-s subsets S of lambda_min(sum_{i in S} theta_i theta_i^T)

conditions: action set is the unit ball B_2^d at all rounds
M = R = rho = 1 (norm bound on theta_i, sub-Gaussian parameter, regulariser)
protected vectors span an s-dimensional subspace (Assumption 3.2)

source.label: thm:known_subspace_dim
source.quote: If we have $\mathcal{A}_t=\mathcal{B}_2^d$, the regret of Algorithm \ref{algorithm:protectedLUCB} satisfies \mathcal{R}_{[T]} \le 12\sqrt{2}\frac{s+1}{\lambda_{\min}}\sqrt{Td\log(1+\frac{TL}{d})}\sqrt{\beta_T\left(\frac{\delta}{2(L+1)}\right)}+\frac{4608L^3d\big(d\log 6+\log\frac{2L}{\delta}\big)^2}{\lambda_{\min}^2} with probability $1-\delta$ where $\sqrt{\beta_t(\delta)}=R\sqrt{d\log(\tfrac{1}{\delta}+\tfrac{tM^2}{\delta\rho})}+M\rho^{\frac{1}{2}}.$

results.notes: beta_T(delta/(2(L+1))) expanded with M=R=rho=1. Pseudo-regret type sum of gaps, holding w.p. 1-delta. The paper summarises it as O~(s d sqrt T). The algorithm does not use T, so the bound is recorded as anytime. The algorithm needs a non-concave optimisation (Remark 7.1), so compute is not stated.

symbols.lambda_min: largest over size-s subsets S of lambda_min(sum_{i in S} theta_i theta_i^T)

conditions: action set is the unit ball B_2^d at all rounds
protected vectors span an s-dimensional subspace (Assumption 3.2)

source.quote: If we have $\mathcal{A}_t=\mathcal{B}_2^d$, the regret of Algorithm \ref{algorithm:protectedLUCB} satisfies \mathcal{R}_{[T]} \le 2\sqrt{((\frac{3\sqrt{s}}{\lambda_{\min}}M+1)^2\beta_T(\frac{\delta}{2(L+1)})+M^2)(s+1)Td\log (1+\frac{TL}{d\rho})}+\frac{1152L^3MR^2(M+R)^2d\big(d\log 6+\log\frac{2L}{\delta}\big)^2}{\lambda_{\min}^2} with probability $1-\delta$ where $\sqrt{\beta_t(\delta)}=R\sqrt{d\log((1+\frac{tM^2}{\rho})/\delta)}+M\rho^{\frac{1}{2}}.$

results.notes: Appendix version of Theorem 5.2 with explicit M, R, rho. Mapping: M -> S, R -> sigma, rho -> lam. The constants are inconsistent with Theorem 5.2 inside the paper itself (e.g. rho vs sqrt(rho) in beta, the power of M in the core-set term).

conditions: hard instance pair with d=2, s=L=1, theta_0 = u_{pi/2 - alpha}, theta_1 in {u_0, u_{-alpha}}, alpha = T^{-1/4}
action set each round is {u_{pi-alpha}, u_{2alpha}} or {u_{pi-alpha}, u_{2alpha}, u_{pi-3alpha}} with equal probability
Gaussian noise used implicitly in the KL computation

source.label: thm:hardness
source.quote: There is an instance of the Protected Linear Bandit problem such that any algorithm incurs a regret of $\Omega(T^{\frac{3}{4}})$.

results.notes: The proof (Appendix, Theorem 11.1 restates the same theorem) gives max{R_1,R_2} >= e^{-21}/16 * T^{3/4} for T >= 256. The paper elsewhere says this holds for 'consistent' algorithms, but the theorem states any algorithm. The optimal action changes with the available action set, so the comparator is the per-round best action.
